text:
Jordan Lee: FYI ran into dup-create when using the async Python client + timeout retries. app hits our create endpoint twice for a single user action.
Jordan Lee: repro is small — async + short timeout + server 502 during streaming then the SDK retries but idempotency header isn't preserved.
Jordan Lee: stack/log snippet: 
```
2026-03-20T10:12:03Z ERROR request failed: httpx.ReadTimeout
2026-03-20T10:12:03Z INFO retrying request attempt=2 reason=ReadTimeout
2026-03-20T10:12:03Z INFO outbound headers: X-Idempotency-Key: 5f2a...c1
2026-03-20T10:12:03Z INFO outbound headers: X-Idempotency-Key: <missing>
2026-03-20T10:12:04Z INFO upstream response: 201 Created id=abc123
2026-03-20T10:12:05Z INFO upstream response: 201 Created id=def456  # duplicate
```
Jordan Lee: so first attempt had idempotency key, but on retry the header got lost (or replaced).
Priya Nair: ouch. do you pass idempotency via kwarg or rely on auto-generated token?
Jordan Lee: we pass idempotency_key=str(uuid4()) on the call. but looking at the client code, the retry logic does a shallow merge of request metadata and seems to call into the transport which regenerates headers for the new call.
Max Chen: is this the async client or sync? any difference in behavior?
Jordan Lee: async only so far (httpx.AsyncClient path). sync code path appears to preserve headers.
Clare O'Neill: could be related to the buffer/stream reset code — for async we rebuild the request object and IIRC headers come from RequestBuilder which consults a per-call context.
Priya Nair: can you paste the minimal repro? will try locally.
Jordan Lee: repro gist (sanitized):
```
import asyncio, uuid
from redwood import AsyncClient

async def main():
    c = AsyncClient(api_key="redacted", retry=RetryPolicy(max_retries=3, backoff=0.1))
    async with c:
        key = uuid.uuid4().hex
        resp = await c.create_resource(payload={"name":"x"}, idempotency_key=key, timeout=0.25)
        print(resp)

asyncio.run(main())
```
This reliably triggers a duplicate when the server returns intermittent 502s during streaming.
Max Chen: thanks. confirms it's not user bug.
Max Chen: likely root cause: on retry we call internal _prepare_request which drops idempotency header if idempotency_key is stored only in request._metadata and not copied onto the new Request.
Clare O'Neill: two fixes: 1) ensure Retry layer serializes/attaches idempotency_key to the new request headers before sending; 2) make SDK treat idempotency_key as an immutable per-call value (store on context) so any regen code doesn't accidentally override.
Priya Nair: agree. also we should document async caveat in changelog and add a regression test that simulates a streaming timeout + 502 to assert only one create happens.
Jordan Lee: open to picking this up. quick patch idea: in retry.py preserve request.context['idempotency_key'] and copy into prepared.headers['X-Idempotency-Key'] before each retry.
Clare O'Neill: watch out for typing: request.context is typed as Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] in types.py, so mutation may require changing types to MutableMapping or explicitly creating a copy — tests will catch it.
Max Chen: also check backoff logic: current default backoff is constant 0.1, maybe switch to decorrelated jitter for high parallelism. This could reduce retry storms.
Jordan Lee: created GH draft issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/1057 (private). added repro and suggested patch.
Priya Nair: can you include a unit/integration test snippet that fakes server behavior? sample: use httpx.MockTransport to return ReadTimeout first then 201, assert only one upstream create recorded.
Jordan Lee: yep will do. quick pseudo:
```
async def test_idemp_preserved(monkeypatch):
    calls = []
    async def handler(req):
        calls.append(req.headers.get('X-Idempotency-Key'))
        if len(calls) == 1:
            raise httpx.ReadTimeout('simulated')
        return httpx.Response(201, json={"id":"ok"})

    transport = httpx.MockTransport(handler)
    client = AsyncClient(transport=transport, retry=RetryPolicy(max_retries=2))
    async with client:
        await client.create_resource(..., idempotency_key='fixed')
    assert calls == ['fixed','fixed']
```
Jordan Lee: that assertion will fail today because second value is None.
Clare O'Neill: good test. add a variant for when user does NOT set idempotency_key (auto-generated) to ensure auto-key remains stable for the whole call.
Max Chen: also flagging API ergonomics: make idempotency_key param typed Optional[str] and document fallback for server-side idempotency too. typing currently uses Any which is noisy.
Priya Nair: I can review the PR. Jordan do you want code owner for retry layer to assign?
Jordan Lee: yes please, assign to me. I'll push patch + tests today.
ci-bot: build queued for branch jordan/idempotency-retry-fix # test-infra
Max Chen: once merged, we should ship a small patch release and add a note to SDK release notes about the bug + workaround.
Priya Nair: thanks Jordan. super helpful repro and test plan. :thumbsup:
Jordan Lee: np, will update issue with PR link when ready.
